pos.personaBrief: His Colombia and Nacional pursued 'posesión con progresión' and short-passing toque (Semana, La Grinta), a team that never gave the ball away, though it could sit back and counter against Argentina.

pro.personaBrief: Centre-backs circulate the ball and midfielders drop to receive for the first passes (La Grinta); short-passing retention with a threat of pace in the final third (WSC).

est.personaBrief: Zonal order that allows disorder with the ball, total football with everyone progressing close together (Coaches' Voice, Semana).

lar.personaBrief: A near-diamond 4-4-2 (La Grinta) with creative midfielders, Valderrama, Rincon, and short combinations through the centre.

blo.personaBrief: Dutch-inspired high pressing and ball recovery with pressing by sequences rather than all-pitch (FourFourTwo, La Grinta, WSC); never a deep block.

mar.personaBrief: Zonal marking with holistic content, 'defensa en zona' as defensive modernity (El Pais, La Grinta, Trivela).

pla.personaBrief: Imposed his own zonal total football model at Nacional and Colombia, rejecting the earlier 'desactivar al rival' approach; went to win even when a draw sufficed vs Germany.

res.personaBrief: Contrasts himself with Bilardo's neutralising: 'salimos a crear', played to win against Germany needing only a draw; tactics as the soul of football with a sense.

sis.personaBrief: A collective order built on technically gifted players like Valderrama and Asprilla, who were allowed to create, with the group ringfenced and duties for all.

jog.personaBrief: Very high technical quality shared by the whole team (La Grinta); the creative number 10 was central, with pace only as a final-third weapon.

bas.personaBrief: Built Nacional and Colombia on home-grown criollos, up to nine Nacional players like Ajax for the Netherlands; mixed youth like Cordoba with established stars.

lid.personaBrief: Humanist leader: poetry, education and dress counselling for players, ringfenced environment, group soul in 2001.
